title: Northbridge Logistics — discovery & integration scratchpad
content:
High-level: Northbridge Logistics — potential pilot for TMS augmentation. Customer is a mid-market 3PL (warehouse + regional freight lanes) interested in automating freight quoting, carrier triage, and exception triage via LLM-powered assistant integrated into their operator UI.

Call notes (2026-02-24, 11:00 PST)
Attendees: Maya (me), Bryan (SE), Ana (AE), Tom Rivera (Head of Ops, Northbridge), Priya Shah (SRE lead), Mark E. (Platform/IT)

Quick impressions: cautious but pragmatic. Main drivers are throughput (many quoting calls), predictability (cost budgeting) and data control (customer PII, contract rates). They like Redwood’s model-routing and Dedicated option for predictability.

Requirements stated (paraphrased):
- Throughput: expect 10k quote requests/day in pilot, peak bursts ~300 req/min. Typical prompt length ~700 tokens (context + conversation).
- Latency target: 500–800ms p50 for short responses, p95 < 2s for the majority of flows.
- Data residency: US-only for now.
- Security: must support VPC Private deployment option with KMS integration (HSM optional).
- Audit: per-request logging and ability to redact PII before storage.
- Model determinism: want reproducible outputs for billing and auditability (seeded generations + ability to pin model versions).
- Fallbacks: on high load prefer graceful degradation to cached responses or smaller model instead of failing the request.
- SLA: initial ask is 99.5% uptime for production pilot.

Gotchas / potential blockers:
- Their platform uses an older OAuth flow and on-prem identity proxy — sign-in is a little custom. Needs IdP integration (SAML/OIDC) + service account for Redwood console access.
- Contract rate tables are PII-ish, but also must be queried in real-time during quote generation. We need to discuss whether to keep that data behind their infra (preferred) and use Redwood Private / Dedicated with prefix caching, or ship encrypted rate snapshots to our hosted API (not preferred).
- Their infra team is strict about outbound rules — VPC peering approach will require network review; they may prefer on-prem Private package.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement asked product team to estimate monthly unit cost under 10k req/day. Need a rough cost model to include batching and quantization options.

Integration notes (technical):
- Preferred architecture (first pass): Northbridge runs Redwood Private in their AWS account (VPC), exposes internal endpoints. App servers call Redwood Private endpoints for generation and embedding. KV/prefix cache remains in their VPC (Redis). KMS: use AWS KMS key for model request encryption.
- Alternate: Redwood Dedicated with a VPC peering + private link to their VPC and strict logging redaction rules.
- Key endpoints: generation (chat) for operator assistant, embeddings API for search/reranking of SOWs + contract clauses.
- Auth: service-to-service mTLS + short-lived tokens. Need to confirm their RBAC mapping (which Redwood token -> which operator role).

Pilot success metrics suggested by customer:
- 80% of basic quotes auto-generated without manual intervention after 2 weeks
- Avg operator handling time down 30%
- Token cost per quote < $0.12 (they asked for explicit cost per quote)
- No PII leak incidents, audit logs available with redaction

Action items / next steps (owners + rough ETA):
- Bryan: build initial cost estimate (per-token + infra) for 10k/day profile including options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Due 2026-03-03.
- Maya: schedule 1-hr tech deep-dive with Priya + Mark to map network constraints and IdP details. Proposed 2026-03-05.
- Ana: collect and share sample rate-table schema (anonymized) and typical query patterns (fields + cardinality). Due 2026-03-02.
- Bryan -> infra: sketch Dedicated topology (autoscale plan + fallback variant model) and quantify expected p95 latency under burst. Due 2026-03-06.
- Maya: open INF ticket for KMS integration options and docs + link to pilot Confluence. INF-4821 created.

Open questions we need answered (for RFP/procurement):
1) Can they accept periodic (nightly) encrypted snapshots of rate tables behind a customer-managed bucket, or must every quote read live data? (affects latency and architecture)
2) Which IdP flows are supported currently (SAML 2.0 only?) — get SP metadata and test account.
3) Are there compliance requirements beyond SOC2 for this pilot (e.g., HITRUST not applicable, but they have freight contracts with gov agencies)?
4) What are their retention windows for logs and audit traces? (we need to align RBAC + console access policies)

Notes to self (SE perspective):
- When we price, include explicit split for tokens vs infra (reserved GPU hours) vs extra ops (network setup). They will try to negotiate to a single line-item.
- Suggest pilot uses 7B quantized model for cost/latency baseline + fallback to 13B for edge cases. Redwood Optimize can run evals on their prompt set to determine quality delta.
- Pre-canned prompts: create template for quoting flow with explicit instructions to mask customer PII before logging (e.g., replace account numbers with <ACCOUNT_REDACTED>).
- For deterministic billing reproducibility, call out requirement for pinned model + temperature=0 + top_p fixed and store model_version in logs.

Meeting excerpts I want to capture verbatim (for legal/procurement):
- Tom R.: "We need predictable costs. If you surprise us with token variance we won't be able to forecast freight margins."
- Priya: "Our security team won't allow additional outbound rules without a network architecture review and a signed data handling addendum."

Quick architecture sketch (notes):
- Northbridge app -> internal API -> Redwood Private endpoint (in their VPC)
  - Redis prefix cache (customer-managed)
  - KMS (AWS, customer key)
  - Audit logs delivered to S3 bucket with lifecycle policy (30d warm, long-term archive 1yr)
  - Health checks and canary traffic routed to smaller model during maintenance windows

Risks / Mitigation:
- Risk: procurement drags on due to legal ask for data handling addendum. Mitigation: provide draft AAD with minimal scope and show precedent with other pilots.
- Risk: under-provisioned dedicated capacity leads to degraded p95. Mitigation: propose conservative reserved capacity for first 30 days and autoscale burst with pre-authorized buffer.

Draft messaging for next customer email (short):
"Thanks Tom/Priya — good convo today. We've started a short pilot plan that includes a Private deployment in your VPC or a Dedicated option with VPC peering. Bryan will share cost estimates by 3/3 and Maya will follow up to schedule a technical deep-dive. We'll also send a short checklist of items we need from your infra team (IdP metadata, sample rate table, egress rules)."

Low-priority ideas (notes):
- Batch quote generation overnight for low-priority lanes to reduce peak cost.
- Use embeddings + sparse retrieval to avoid shipping full contract texts into prompt each time.

End of scratchpad. Keep this in users/ (private notes) until legal approves sharing of demo artifacts.
